story: मैंने 5 अक्टूबर 2026 को ऑनलाइन 3,200 रुपये का मिक्सर ग्राइंडर खरीदा। वह टूटा हुआ था। मैंने 8 अक्टूबर को लौटा दिया लेकिन पैसे वापस नहीं मिले।

rules.name: consumer_limitation
rules.message: File your consumer complaint before 08 Oct 2028 (700 days left). This counts 2 years from 08 Oct 2026 (the date they refused; if they refused earlier, your deadline is earlier). Don't wait for the last date. Sending a letter or calling the helpline does NOT pause this clock.
rules.label: Last date to file your consumer complaint

rules.name: forum_and_fee
rules.message: You paid Rs 3,200, so the complaint goes to the District Consumer Commission, with no filing fee. You can file in the district where you live or work, online at e-jagriti.gov.in. You don't need a lawyer to file.
rules.label: Where to file

rules.name: free_first_steps
rules.message: Two free steps often work first: (1) a written complaint to the seller's or platform's grievance officer, (2) the National Consumer Helpline: call 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915.
rules.label: Try these first

answer.summary: You bought a broken mixer grinder online for Rs 3,200 and returned it, but the seller did not give you a refund.

claims.text: You are a consumer under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 because you bought goods for personal use and not for resale or commercial purposes.
The broken mixer grinder counts as a 'defect' under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
Refusing to take back defective goods and refund your money is an unfair trade practice under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
You can file a complaint in the District Consumer Commission where you live or work.
Because your amount is Rs 3,200, your complaint has no filing fee.
You must file your complaint within two years from the date the seller refused your refund.

next_steps.action: Call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915.
next_steps.why: This is a free first step to try to get your money back before filing a formal case.

next_steps.action: Send a written complaint to the seller or platform's grievance officer.
next_steps.why: This creates a paper trail showing you tried to resolve the issue directly.

next_steps.action: File an online complaint at e-jagriti.gov.in.
next_steps.why: You can file your consumer complaint online without a lawyer for free.

support.text: You are a consumer under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 because you bought goods for personal use and not for resale or commercial purposes.
support.reason: The law text defines 'consumer' as a person who buys goods for consideration (paid or promised) and explicitly excludes 'a person who obtains such goods for resale or for any commercial purpose.' The sentence correctly applies this rule by stating the person bought goods for personal use and not for resale or commercial purposes, which matches the statutory definition and exclusion.

support.text: The broken mixer grinder counts as a 'defect' under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
support.reason: The law text defines 'defect' as 'any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard.' A broken mixer grinder would constitute such a fault or imperfection, directly falling within this definition.

support.text: Refusing to take back defective goods and refund your money is an unfair trade practice under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
support.reason: The law text explicitly states that 'refusing, after selling goods or rendering services, to take back or withdraw defective goods or to withdraw or discontinue deficient services and to refund the consideration thereof... within the period stipulated in the bill or cash memo or receipt or in the absence of such stipulation, within a period of thirty days' is an unfair trade practice. The sentence directly quotes this rule without adding any unstated conditions.

support.text: You can file a complaint in the District Consumer Commission where you live or work.
support.reason: The law text provides multiple jurisdictional bases for filing a complaint (a, b, c, d), but does NOT state that a complainant can file in their local District Commission solely based on where they live or work. Clause (d) requires the complainant to 'reside or personally works for gain' - 'personally works for gain' is not the same as 'works' in general, and 'lives' is not 'lives or works' - but more critically, the sentence oversimplifies by stating 'lives or works' as a blanket right without acknowledging this is only one of four alternative bases and may require permission in some cases. However, the main issue is that the sentence presents 'lives or works' as the sole or primary basis, while the law text lists it as one of four alternatives (d). Actually, re-reading: the sentence says 'where you live or work' - the law text says 'resides or personally works for gain' under (d). The sentence 'works' is broader than 'personally works for gain', so this adds a condition not in the text. Also, the sentence doesn't mention this is only one of four bases. But the key issue is 'works' vs 'personally works for gain' - the sentence is broader.

support.text: You can file a complaint in the District Consumer Commission where you live or work.
support.reason: The law text [CPA2019_s35_1] describes who MAY file a complaint (the consumer, recognised consumer association, etc.) but does NOT specify WHERE to file it. The sentence incorrectly attributes the jurisdictional rule from s34 to s35. The 'where you live or work' rule comes from s34(2)(d), not s35(1).

support.text: Because your amount is Rs 3,200, your complaint has no filing fee.
support.reason: The law text [CPFEE_r7] states 'No fee where the consideration paid is up to Rs 5 lakh.' The sentence applies this rule to Rs 3,200, which is within the 'up to Rs 5 lakh' threshold, so no filing fee applies.

support.text: You must file your complaint within two years from the date the seller refused your refund.
support.reason: The law text [CPA2019_s69] states that complaints must be filed 'within two years from the date on which the cause of action has arisen.' The sentence correctly applies this two-year time limit, and the cause of action is the date the seller refused the refund.

rendered.summary: आपने ऑनलाइन ₹3,200 का एक खराब मिक्सर ग्राइंडर खरीदा और उसे वापस कर दिया, लेकिन सेलर ने आपको रिफंड नहीं दिया।
claims: आप Consumer Protection Act, 2019 के तहत एक कंज्यूमर हैं क्योंकि आपने सामान पर्सनल इस्तेमाल के लिए खरीदा है, न कि दोबारा बेचने या कमर्शियल काम के लिए।
खराब मिक्सर ग्राइंडर Consumer Protection Act, 2019 के तहत एक 'डिफेक्ट' (खराबी) माना जाता है।
खराब सामान वापस लेने और आपके पैसे रिफंड करने से मना करना Consumer Protection Act, 2019 के तहत एक अनफेयर ट्रेड प्रैक्टिस है।
आप उस डिस्ट्रिक्ट कंज्यूमर कमीशन में शिकायत दर्ज कर सकते हैं जहाँ आप रहते हैं या काम करते हैं।
क्योंकि आपकी रकम ₹3,200 है, इसलिए आपकी शिकायत फाइल करने की कोई फीस नहीं है।
सेलर द्वारा आपका रिफंड देने से मना करने की तारीख से दो साल के अंदर आपको अपनी शिकायत दर्ज करनी ही होगी।
next_steps: नेशनल कंज्यूमर हेल्पलाइन 1915 पर कॉल करें या 8800001915 पर WhatsApp करें। — फॉर्मल केस फाइल करने से पहले अपने पैसे वापस पाने की कोशिश करने के लिए यह एक फ्री पहला कदम है।
सेलर या प्लेटफॉर्म के ग्रीवांस ऑफिसर को एक लिखित शिकायत भेजें। — इससे एक पेपर ट्रेल बनता है जो दिखाता है कि आपने सीधे तौर पर मामला सुलझाने की कोशिश की।
e-jagriti.gov.in पर ऑनलाइन शिकायत फाइल करें। — आप बिना वकील के फ्री में अपनी कंज्यूमर शिकायत ऑनलाइन फाइल कर सकते हैं।
questions_for_user: आपने मिक्सर ग्राइंडर किस ऑनलाइन प्लेटफॉर्म या सेलर से खरीदा था?
सेलर ने आपका रिफंड देने से मना करने का क्या कारण बताया?
क्या आपके पास अभी भी ओरिजिनल बिल, रिटर्न कन्फर्मेशन, या सेलर के साथ कोई ईमेल/मैसेज हैं?

Date: 08 November 2026
From: [FILL: your full name], [FILL: your full postal address]
To: [FILL: name of the other party], [FILL: their address / registered office / email]

Subject: Demand for refund

On 05 October 2026 I paid Rs 3,200 to you for [FILL: product/service and order number]. [FILL: what went wrong, e.g. product defective / service not provided]. Despite my requests, including on 08 October 2026, you have not refunded the amount.

I request a full refund of Rs 3,200 within 15 days of receiving this letter.

If the refund is not made, I intend to file a complaint before the District Consumer Commission under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, without further notice to you.

I have the following records: [FILL: receipts, chats, emails, bank statements].

Yours faithfully,
[FILL: your name and signature]

draft_notes:
How to send it:
1. Find their correct address in the invoice, order page, or the seller's 'grievance officer' details on the website/app.
2. Fill every [FILL] slot. Remove anything that isn't true - only state facts you can prove.
3. Send by Speed Post and keep the receipt and the tracking proof of delivery. Also send a copy by email or WhatsApp and keep a screenshot.
4. Wait 15 days. Sending this letter does NOT stop any legal time limit - file your claim/complaint before the deadline shown, even if they haven't replied.
5. Free help to check the letter: legal aid 15100 or Tele-Law 14454.

Laws this letter relies on: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.69 (Two-year limitation and condonation); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.34(2) (Where to file: District Commission); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.35(1) (Who may file a complaint; e-filing)
